summary: Wrote pnr/floorplan.json (core_utilization_pct 45, inside the 30-65 range) with a reason for utilization, pins, power grid and clock/reset, and pnr/pin_order.cfg placing all 21 ports: load_data[7:0], load, enable, up_down on #W; count[7:0] on #E; clk on #N; rst_n on #S. No tool was run by me; the floorplan, pin-order parsing and PDN checks are for the runtime to run and confirm.
assumptions: All inputs are synchronous to clk (spec REQ-011), so no pin needs to sit next to a specific synchronizer; side choice is driven only by data flow.
Cell area from reports/synth_tool.json (709.4304 um2) is the standard-cell area the flow uses for FP_CORE_UTIL sizing; at 45% the core is about 1576 um2 (roughly 40 um x 40 um).

OpenLane's pin-order parser matches each pattern against the whole pin name (implicit full match), so pattern `load` matches only the `load` port and not `load_data[*]`; if it matches by prefix, `load` would also match load_data and the runtime check will report it.
The PDK default SKY130 PDN (sky130A / sky130_fd_sc_hd defaults in OpenLane) is used unchanged, as the task states; strap pitch and width are not edited.
open_issues: Spec open question on STA corners and sky130A release is unresolved (G1 review); it does not change the floorplan choice.

The design is very small (about 40 um x 40 um core); the PDK default PDN may leave few straps over the core. The runtime PDN connectivity / unpowered-row check must confirm every row is powered; if not, the fix is a die-size or PDN-pitch change for a human to approve since pnr_ranges.yaml has no strap ranges.

self_assessment.reason: Utilization and pin assignment are straightforward and every port is covered exactly once by the patterns, but the `load` vs `load_data.*` disambiguation depends on the OpenLane parser's full-match behaviour, and PDN coverage on a tiny core can only be confirmed by the real tool run.
